newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult doctor says guru ordered subway attack.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult doctor says guru ordered subway attack.

text.p: The former doctor of the Japanese doomsday cult accused of gassing Tokyo subways told a court on Thursday he joined in last year's deadly attack because he believed it was ordered by cult leader Shoko Asahara.

Ikuo Hayashi, 49, ex-doctor of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), testifying against Asahara at Tokyo District Court, said he believed the cult was itself under nerve gas attack and never questioned the subway orders.
"I feel embarassed to say this, but I truly believed it and there is nothing I can do about it because that is the truth," Hayashi told the court.
Asahara, 41, whose real name is Chizuo Matsumoto, is on trial in 17 cases, including the subway gassing that killed 12 people and injured thousands on March 20, 1995.
Hayashi, the fourth top cult official to testify against the guru in recent trial sessions, said Asahara had also ordered murders on several other occassions.

"Asahara ordered murder. I heard him use the (Sanskrit) word 'poa' which means to kill a human being, three times," Hayashi said, referring to an abortive attack on a religious rival and the killing of a rebellious cult follower.
Asahara, who has refused to enter a plea against any of the charges, sat in the courtroom with his eyes closed and fell asleep, forcing his lawyers to wake him.
